drafted_from: tool row in tools/track-and-compare-movement/tool-rows.json, do-work/estimate_pose.py and test/test_estimate_pose.py (read from code and test; no pose model run here)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the poses of the people in /work/serve.mp4 with my pose model /work/models/pose.pt and write the track to /work/poses/serve.json." It reads the tool's row and runs estimate_pose.py on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads video or pose files on the person's own computer and writes a new file or folder beside them.
instructions: 1. Have the video and a pose model file you downloaded (an ultralytics pose checkpoint); ultralytics is AGPL-3.0, so check its licence suits your use, then install numpy, opencv-python and ultralytics in a Python 3.10 or later environment.

2. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video} and runs its `run` command with --video, --out, --checkpoint and optionally --device, --conf (0.3 if you say nothing) and --max-frames (0 for the whole video).

3. Read the last line: {"result": {out, persons, frames, cached}} or {"error": ...}. The file holds, for each person kept as one track id, per frame 17 joints as [x, y, confidence]; a joint not found is [0, 0, 0].
4. A second run with the same video bytes and the same checkpoint returns at once with cached true. Use the track with tool:line-up-two-movements or tool:plan-a-side-by-side-movement-comparison.

worked_examples.title: Run again on a video that already has its track
worked_examples.ask: Read the poses of the people in /work/serve.mp4 with my pose model.
worked_examples.given: From tools/track-and-compare-movement/test/test_estimate_pose.py (a track made from the same video and checkpoint is returned without a model): /work/poses/serve.json already holds a pose.keypoints.v1 track with one person (track_id 1), 4 video frames and the digest of /work/serve.mp4 and checkpoint /work/models/pose.pt. Command: motion-env/bin/python tools/track-and-compare-movement/do-work/estimate_pose.py --video /work/serve.mp4 --out /work/poses/serve.json --checkpoint /work/models/pose.pt --device cpu --conf 0.3 --max-frames 0.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"out": "/work/poses/serve.json", "persons": 1, "frames": 4, "cached": true}} A first run on a new video does the same work with a pose model and prints cached false with the counts it found.

worked_examples.title: A missing video is refused with what to change
worked_examples.given: I ran estimate_pose.py with --video /work/none.mp4 --out /work/t.json --checkpoint /work/models/pose.pt where /work/none.mp4 does not exist (see test/test_estimate_pose.py, test_a_missing_video_or_checkpoint_says_what_to_change); it exits 2.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"error": "the video is not a file on this computer: /work/none.mp4"} A missing checkpoint instead answers "the pose checkpoint is not a file on this computer: <path>; give the path of a downloaded pose model".
